Source ticket: MAG-15 — https://linear.app/magus-monitor/issue/MAG-15/battery-consumed-graph

RM28 tier 1. Create the charge_gaps table (days whose battery math does not add up because a charge record is missing or incomplete) plus its GapWriter write port, and add SuperchargerSessionsByVehicleBetween to the SuperchargerReader port. Roadmap decisions D3, D7, D7a, D7b, D9, D12 bind this change.

decisions.decision: DATABASE DESIGN GATE PASSED. The user reviewed and approved the charge_gaps schema, its rationale and its index plan, with one change: the date column is renamed to gap_date.
decisions.why: A bare `date` would be the only non-descriptive date column in the schema (cf. charged_on, captured_date, charge_start_date_time) and is a Postgres col_name_keyword. The Go domain field stays ChargeGap.Date to avoid stuttering.

decisions.decision: idx_charge_gaps_account (account_id, gap_date DESC) is KEPT despite serving a notification feature that does not exist yet.
decisions.why: Leader flagged it as speculative on a table that stays tiny. The user chose to keep it rather than defer; it is cheap and the read pattern is declared in the design.

decisions.decision: Collapsed the five computed depends_on waves into two dispatches: wave 1 = T1-T6 (implementation), wave 2 = T7-T8 (DB tests + docs).
decisions.why: Every computed wave is a serial single-module chain, so five dispatches would re-read the doc pack five times for zero parallelism. Tests stay last: they cannot compile before the migration and sqlc types exist.

decisions.decision: Leader added the missing SuperchargerSessionsByVehicleBetween method to the test doubles in internal/battery and internal/gateway/handlers, as panic-on-call stubs.
decisions.why: Adding a port method broke go vet in two sibling modules. Cross-module integration is the leader’s job, not a sandboxed worker’s. Panic, not nil, so an unexpected call fails loudly.

decisions.decision: Corrected design.md test-contract scenario (d): "ordered before S1" changed to "ordered after S1".
decisions.why: The bullet contradicted its own parenthetical and scenario (c). Query orders by charge_stop_date_time ASC, so a later stop sorts later. Authoring bug in the artifact, not the code.

decisions.decision: Leader added the missing charge_gaps row to the root README's per-module data-ownership table.
decisions.why: V12 asked for a real confirmation, not an assumption. The table lists every table each module owns; omitting charge_gaps would breach the project's docs-track-structural-change rule. Root README is leader-owned, outside the worker sandbox.

decisions.decision: R1-1 accepted and fixed in this change rather than backlogged: T9 adds regression tests for the two untested spec.md scenarios.
decisions.why: User's call from three offered options. A spec requirement with no test tends to stay untested, and window/vehicle scoping is the port's core safety property.

decisions.decision: Leader replaced the worker's self-reported T9 timestamps with real clock readings.
decisions.why: The worker stated its timestamps were session-relative estimates with no clock source, and dated them 2026-08-15. Timestamps are leader-owned; fabricated ones would misrepresent the record.

review.brief: Review RM28-telemetry-add-charge-gap-storage (telemetry, commits 9bdbc02..d24ac05 off 874820f). Validate: (1) MODULE BOUNDARY - internal/telemetry imports only account + tesla public packages + its own db; no other module's internals; pgtype confined to service.go/mapping.go (not gap_writer.go). (2) DB-vs-CONFIRMED-DESIGN - the shipped charge_gaps DDL must match design.md AND user gate decisions G1 (column named gap_date, NOT date) and G2 (idx_charge_gaps_account kept). Any mismatch is a BLOCKER. Exactly two indexes; nothing added on supercharger_sessions. UpsertChargeGap's ON CONFLICT SET must not touch created_at (D-Table2). (3) TEST-CONTRACT - the DB integration tests must assert the expectations design.md authored UP FRONT (scenarios a-e), not whatever the implementation happens to do. Scenario (d) was corrected mid-flight (G5, ordered AFTER S1) - verify the test matches the corrected contract and the corrected contract matches query.sql's ORDER BY. (4) SPEC/TASKS COVERAGE - specs/telemetry/spec.md requirements all implemented; no task or acceptance criterion was edited, weakened or deleted (append-only). (5) PERFORMANCE-PROFILE (read-heavy) compliance within the module boundary. (6) TWO LEADER-FLAGGED ITEMS TO JUDGE INDEPENDENTLY, do not rubber-stamp: (a) V2 is UNTICKED - gofmt -l reports 14 files; leader claims all 14 are pre-existing at base 874820f and untouched here; verify that claim. (b) V11 is PARTIALLY MET - the leader edited two files OUTSIDE the module sandbox, internal/battery/reader_test.go and internal/gateway/handlers/supercharger_test.go, adding panic-on-call stubs for the new port method (G4). Judge whether that was the right call, whether panic-not-nil is right, and whether it belongs in this change. (7) ANTI-GAMING - no self-approved statuses, no weakened criteria. TEST-EXECUTION-POLICY (verbatim, binds you too): Claude writes tests but never runs the suite - never go test ./..., make test, make test-with-db or make check. It MAY run go build ./..., go vet ./..., gofmt -l, make build, make vet, make bins, and the standalone guards make ui-guard / make i18n-guard / make money-guard. The owner runs the suite and reports results; work that is complete but unexecuted is awaiting-user-verification, never done, and a passing suite is recorded as the owner's report, never claimed by the assistant. SIGNAL PROVENANCE: go build, go vet, gofmt -l and openspec validate --strict were ASSISTANT-run (all clean except the pre-existing gofmt files). `make test` was USER-run and USER-reported passing - that is the owner's verification, not the assistant's. Judge test QUALITY by READING the tests; do not run the suite.

findings.note: spec.md's two ADDED-requirement scenarios 'Reconciliation only affects the reconciled window' (a charge_gaps row on a day OUTSIDE the window being reconciled must be untouched) and 'Ledger rows for different vehicles are independent' (same account, two tesla_ids) have no dedicated regression test. design.md's own authored Test Contract (a)-(e) never enumerated either as a scenario, so no task/test omitted anything promised — this is a gap between spec.md's scenario list and design.md's test-contract transcription, not a gaming or coverage-claim issue. I independently verified both behaviors hold against the code: gap_writer.go's ChargeGapDatesByVehicleBetween/DeleteChargeGap/UpsertChargeGap calls (internal/telemetry/db/query.sql) are all scoped by account_id AND tesla_id AND a gap_date bound to [start,end], so window- and vehicle-isolation are structural, not incidental. Non-blocking; worth a follow-up regression test given this is the port's core safety property (a caller bug that widened the internal existing-rows query could silently wipe unrelated days without any test catching it).

Files touched outside internal/telemetry: README.md (leader, data-ownership table row), internal/battery/reader_test.go and internal/gateway/handlers/supercharger_test.go (leader, test-only interface-satisfaction stubs, G4). internal/battery production code untouched.
verified.db_vs_confirmed_design: Migration 20260815000002_add_charge_gaps.sql diffed byte-for-byte against design.md's Schema section: column is gap_date (G1 honored), idx_charge_gaps_account (account_id, gap_date DESC) present (G2 honored), exactly one CREATE INDEX statement in the migration (the UNIQUE constraint supplies the second implicit index — two total, no third), no migration or query touches supercharger_sessions. UpsertChargeGap's ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET refreshes only vin, missing_charging_type, updated_at — created_at is absent, matching D-Table2.
verified.test_contract: db_gap_writer_integration_test.go and db_supercharger_between_integration_test.go implement scenarios (a)-(e) matching design.md's authored expected values, including byte-for-byte created_at preservation, updated_at advancement, per-day delete precision, empty-flagged-set clearing, and full-call rejection on mis-scoped entries. Scenario (d) test asserts got[0]=S1, got[1]=S5 (ascending stop-time order), matching the G5-corrected contract text ('ordered after S1') and query.sql's ORDER BY charge_stop_date_time ASC — verified consistent.
verified.spec_tasks_coverage: Both spec.md requirements (Charge Gap Ledger; Supercharger Session Read Port modification) are implemented per the code read. tasks.md revision history (git log -p) shows only checkbox toggles ([ ]->[x]) and appended *Leader-verified*/*Leader note* annotations on V2/V10/V11/V12 — no task or acceptance-criterion title/body text was altered or removed; V2 and V11 were left honestly unticked/partial rather than gamed to done. See R1-1 for the one coverage gap found.
verified.performance_profile: Index Plan (design.md) matches the read-heavy profile: reuses the UNIQUE constraint's own index for the per-vehicle reconciliation path, adds one deliberate account-wide index for a named (if not-yet-built) read pattern, declines a third index on supercharger_sessions for the new bounded query (documented trade-off), and declines a LIMIT on the new query for a reasoned, non-cargo-culted reason. No violation of module-boundary or data-ownership found in the read/write path design.
verified.leader_flagged_6a_gofmt: INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED TRUE. Ran gofmt -l . myself: same 14 files. For each of the 14, git diff 874820f..HEAD -- <file> is empty (byte-identical to base) — confirmed via a loop, not sampling. Separately confirmed every .go file this change DID touch is gofmt-clean (git diff --name-only -- '*.go' | xargs gofmt -l produced no output). go build ./... and go vet ./... also independently re-run clean.
verified.leader_flagged_6b_cross_module_stubs: MY INDEPENDENT JUDGMENT (not a rubber stamp): the right call, correctly scoped and correctly implemented. Extending a public interface (SuperchargerReader) breaks every existing fake implementing it repo-wide at compile time — this is unavoidable and not specific to the pipeline's module sandboxing; it is how Go's structural interfaces work. Deferring the fix to a later change would leave go build/go vet failing across the whole repo between merge and that later change, which is not an option under this project's 'go vet must stay green' signal. The edits are test-only (no production code), minimal (one method each), and correctly attributed to the leader (agentic-workflow.md: 'The lead integrates — wires the modules together... reconciles the slices'), not smuggled into the worker's sandboxed diff. Panic-on-call (not nil) is the RIGHT choice, not just a style pick: it mirrors the pre-existing convention already in both fakes (their existing SuperchargerSessionsByAccount stub in internal/battery/reader_test.go already panics with an identical 'must not be called from RecentEfficiency' message, predating this change) — an unexpected call fails loudly and immediately rather than producing a confusing nil-slice bug three layers away. V11 is correctly left 'partially met' rather than reworded to 'met' — honest self-reporting, not gaming.
